what: Lennox makes heating and air conditioning equipment for American homes and commercial buildings, and sells much of it through its own network of stores rather than independent distributors.
customers: Heating and air conditioning contractors, and commercial building owners, in North America.
money: residential furnaces, air conditioners and heat pumps
moat: Owning the distribution. Selling through its own stores means Lennox keeps the distributor margin and controls how contractors are served, which rivals who sell through wholesalers cannot do.
risks: Replacement demand depends on weather and consumer confidence
Revenue has levelled off at about $5.2B after several years of growth
opportunities: A 15.5% net margin, the best in the industry, and $836M of free cash flow
16 times earnings, cheap relative to Trane and Carrier for a higher margin
Most sales are emergency replacements rather than new buildings, which holds up better in a downturn
watch: Residential volume separate from price, and the margin in the commercial segment.
